tier1.text: A muscular reservoir in the pelvis that stores urine arriving from the kidneys through the ureters.

tier2.text: The urinary bladder is a stretchy, sac-like organ that stores urine and then releases the urine through the urethra, the tube leading to the outside of the body. Urine reaches the bladder through the two ureters, the tubes that carry urine from the kidneys. The bladder sits behind the pubic bone and in front of the rectum; in females, the bladder also lies in front of the uterus. The bladder's inner lining is transitional epithelium, a lining of stacked cells whose top cells change shape in response to urine. When the bladder is empty, its lining has many folds called rugae; the rugae and the transitional epithelium let the bladder expand as it fills. In adults, the volume of urine in the bladder ranges from nearly zero to 500–600 mL. Three openings in the bladder floor, two from the ureters and one into the urethra, mark the corners of a triangle called the trigone. The bladder wall contains the detrusor muscle, whose fibers run in all directions and contract to push urine out of the bladder. Urination starts with stretch sensors in the bladder wall, which send nerve signals to the spinal cord to trigger a reflex. In response, the detrusor muscle contracts while the internal urethral sphincter relaxes; this sphincter is the muscle where the bladder joins the urethra.

sentences.text: The bladder sits behind the pubic bone and in front of the rectum; in females, the bladder also lies in front of the uterus.

quotes.quote: The bladder lies anterior to the uterus in females, posterior to the pubic bone and anterior to the rectum.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The bladder's inner lining is transitional epithelium, a lining of stacked cells whose top cells change shape in response to urine.

quotes.quote: The inner lining of the urinary bladder is a mucous membrane of transitional epithelium that is continuous with that in the ureters.
quotes.citation: SEER Training Modules: Urinary Bladder. U.S. National Institutes of Health, National Cancer Institute.

quotes.quote: transitional epithelium: form of stratified epithelium found in the urinary tract, characterized by an apical layer of cells that change shape in response to the presence of urine
quotes.section: Chapter 4 Key Terms (The Tissue Level of Organization)
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: When the bladder is empty, its lining has many folds called rugae; the rugae and the transitional epithelium let the bladder expand as it fills.

quotes.quote: When the bladder is empty, the mucosa has numerous folds called rugae. The rugae and transitional epithelium allow the bladder to expand as it fills.
quotes.citation: SEER Training Modules: Urinary Bladder. U.S. National Institutes of Health, National Cancer Institute.

sentences.text: In adults, the volume of urine in the bladder ranges from nearly zero to 500–600 mL.

quotes.quote: Volumes in adults can range from nearly zero to 500–600 mL.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Three openings in the bladder floor, two from the ureters and one into the urethra, mark the corners of a triangle called the trigone.

quotes.quote: There is a triangular area, called the trigone, formed by three openings in the floor of the urinary bladder. Two of the openings are from the ureters and form the base of the trigone.
quotes.citation: SEER Training Modules: Urinary Bladder. U.S. National Institutes of Health, National Cancer Institute.

quotes.quote: trigone: area at the base of the bladder marked by the two ureters in the posterior–lateral aspect and the urethral orifice in the anterior aspect oriented like points on a triangle
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: The bladder wall contains the detrusor muscle, whose fibers run in all directions and contract to push urine out of the bladder.

quotes.quote: The smooth muscle fibers are interwoven in all directions and, collectively, these are called the detrusor muscle. Contraction of this muscle expels urine from the bladder.
quotes.citation: SEER Training Modules: Urinary Bladder. U.S. National Institutes of Health, National Cancer Institute.

quotes.quote: detrusor muscle: smooth muscle in the bladder wall; fibers run in all directions to reduce the size of the organ when emptying it of urine
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: Urination starts with stretch sensors in the bladder wall, which send nerve signals to the spinal cord to trigger a reflex.

quotes.quote: Normal micturition is a result of stretch receptors in the bladder wall that transmit nerve impulses to the sacral region of the spinal cord to generate a spinal reflex.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: In response, the detrusor muscle contracts while the internal urethral sphincter relaxes; this sphincter is the muscle where the bladder joins the urethra.

quotes.quote: The resulting parasympathetic neural outflow causes contraction of the detrusor muscle and relaxation of the involuntary internal urethral sphincter.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: internal urinary sphincter: smooth muscle at the juncture of the bladder and urethra; relaxes as the bladder fills to allow urine into the urethra
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
